items.applicant: a transparency activist, co-convenor of the National Campaign for People's Right to Information
items.asked: A copy of any independent appraisal or study on which the Commission decided to begin the SIR across the country in 2025, and the files, notings and records on that decision, with time to inspect them.
items.answer: The Times of India reported that the CPIO pointed to the guidelines of 24 June 2025 and said no further information was available, and The News Minute reported that on first appeal the Commission's Principal Secretary wrote that the Commission had not taken any decision on a nationwide SIR in 2025.
items.quote: Appellant is informed that the Commission has so far not taken any decision on initiating a Special Intensive Revision (SIR) across the country in 2025 and hence no information to be provided in this regard.
items.headline: Who decided on nationwide SIR? EC's RTI response raises questions

items.applicant: My Vote, My Right (a coalition of civil society groups)
items.asked: The definition of 'logical discrepancy' in any official document and the number of notices issued to electors in the 10 States and UTs where the SIR was complete.
items.answer: The News Minute reported that the Commission said the information was not available with it and might be with the CEOs of the States and UTs.
items.quote: The information sought by you is not available in the Commission. It may be available with the Office of the CEO of States/UTs
items.headline: ECI has no record of what constitutes 'logical discrepancy' in SIR, RTI reply shows

items.applicant: a transparency activist, co-convenor of the National Campaign for People's Right to Information
items.asked: The order or notification for the 2003 intensive revision of Bihar's rolls and the guidelines for that revision, including the forms and documents required.
items.answer: Deccan Herald and The Times of India reported that the CPIO sent only the link to the 2025 SIR guidelines of 24 June 2025 and gave nothing on the 2003 revision.
items.quote: The EC did not provide the details sought under RTI and again provided the June 24 order.
items.headline: Election Commission refuses to provide 2003 Bihar SIR order on RTI query

items.asked: All files, notings, correspondence, minutes, presentations and drafts on the SIR ordered on 24 June 2025, and a list of the files recording it.
items.answer: The Reporters' Collective reported that the Commission replied with a link to a page of 'comprehensive instructions' dated 14 July 2025 that the outlet could not open, and did not name any file on the decision.
items.quote: However, in response to our RTI application, the ECI provided a weblink to a back-end page on its website, which cannot be publicly accessed. These, ECI claimed, were “comprehensive instructions” dated July 14, 2025, which were self-explanatory, but we could not access them.
items.headline: A Dead Weblink: The Election Commission of India Demands Citizens' Records but Withholds Its Own Under RTI Law

items.asked: Technical documents on the 'logical discrepancy' module in ERONET used for the West Bengal SIR, its logic and parameters, procurement and testing records, file notings, instructions to EROs, and the number of electors flagged under each sub-category.
items.answer: Deccan Herald (PTI) reported that the Commission held the software questions exempt under Section 8(1)(d), said no module or separate procurement had been made for the West Bengal SIR, and directed the question on flagged electors to the EROs.
items.quote: No separate procurement and development has been made for SIR in West Bengal.
items.headline: TMC's Saket Gokhale says EC 'withholding' details of SIR software, cites RTI response

items.authority: Ministry of Law and Justice, transferred to the Election Commission of India
items.asked: Whether the Commission sought the Law Ministry's legal opinion on the SIR and, if so, the full paper trail of files, correspondence, memos, notes and presentations.
items.answer: The Reporters' Collective reported that the Ministry said it keeps no record of such advice and transferred the request to the Commission, which replied on 20 August 2025 that it had no information.
items.quote: On August 20, 2025, the ECI responded, stating it had no information available.
items.headline: A Dead Weblink: The Election Commission of India Demands Citizens' Records but Withholds Its Own Under RTI Law

items.authority: CEO Bihar, transferred to the 38 DEOs
items.asked: How many times EROs sent speed post notices to absent or shifted electors during the SIR, how many replies they received and how many notices came back undelivered.
items.answer: The Reporters' Collective reported that the CEO sent the application to all 38 district election offices and that after eleven months only the Dulhin Bazar subdivision of Patna and the Hajipur district office had replied, the first saying it sent no speed post notices and the second saying electors were marked from the BLOs' door to door survey.
items.quote: The Dulhin Bazar subdivision of Patna has confirmed that it did not follow the written down existing processes to purge shifted voters. It had not contacted any of the absent or shifted voters via speed post.
items.headline: Did You Follow the Laid Down Rules During SIR? Not in Bihar, Say Election Officials

items.asked: File notings on the decision to begin the second phase of the SIR and the minutes of all meetings held on it.
items.answer: The Wire reported that after a first appeal the Commission supplied two pages of file notings showing the proposal initiated by an Under Secretary on 27 October 2025 and approved the same day, and supplied no minutes of meetings.
items.quote: The CPIO did not provide a response within the statutory time limit. In the first appeal, the CPIO attributed the delay to workload constraints. The RTI application, filed on November 29, 2025, was finally responded to on March 19, 2026 – more than three months after the prescribed period.
items.headline: If Voter Rolls Were Properly Maintained, Would SIR Be Needed? RTI Records Tell the Story.

items.applicant: a Congress Member of Parliament from West Bengal
items.asked: Figures on appeals before the SIR appellate tribunals in West Bengal, received, decided, allowed and rejected, district by district.
items.answer: The Wire reported a 28 page reply, Memo No. 8551/Home (Elec), showing that as of 7 August 2026 the tribunals had received 38,10,620 appeals and decided 82,782, of which 75,443 ended in inclusion and 7,339 in exclusion, with a footnote that the total mixes appeals against inclusion and against exclusion.
items.quote: These include appeals against inclusion and appeals against exclusion.
items.headline: Bengal Tribunal Has So Far Decided Just 2.17% of SIR Appeals; Over 37 Lakh Still in Limbo

items.applicant: a petitioner in the Calcutta High Court
items.asked: The circular or notification under which the SIR was carried out in West Bengal and any record the Commission holds on foreign nationals on the roll.
items.answer: ETV Bharat reported that the CPIO gave no information, that the first appellate authority directed disclosure within seven days and warned on 9 February 2026, and that on 18 March 2026 the Calcutta High Court directed the CPIO to supply the information within seven days.
items.quote: আজ আদালত কমিশনের সিপিআইও-কে সাত দিনের মধ্যে এই তথ্য আমাদের দিতে নির্দেশ দিয়েছে ৷
items.headline: কোন বিজ্ঞপ্তির ভিত্তিতে রাজ্যে SIR, নির্বাচন কমিশনকে জানাতে নির্দেশ হাইকোর্টের

items.authority: Election Commission of India, CEO Delhi, CEO West Bengal
items.asked: The criteria for flagging 'logical discrepancies' and their version history, contracts for ERONET 2.0, ECINET and roll digitisation, Election Commissioners' recorded objections and minutes, data retention and sharing, and State-wise counts of electors excluded, noticed, deleted and restored on appeal.
items.answer: Internet Freedom Foundation said it had filed the applications and would publish the responses and appeal any refusal.
items.quote: We will publish every response we receive, and we will file appeals against any refusal that does not meet the standards of the RTI Act.
items.headline: IFF Filed RTI Applications Seeking What the Election Commission Has Not Disclosed About the SIR
